problems.stem: You have a 5-slide deck. Which version shows structure was built before decoration?
options: Every slide has a gradient background and entrance animations, but the titles read 'Slide 1', 'Slide 2'.
Each slide has an assertion headline (for example 'Sales rose 18% after the redesign') and at most three supporting points; no theme applied yet.
One slide holds a 9-bullet paragraph copied from the report.
The deck uses three different fonts and clip art on every slide.
problems.explanation: Assertion headlines plus limited support are the structure; decoration is deferred until the message arc is clear.

problems.stem: Which note about your draft gives BigAL a structural problem to work on?
options: These slides need to pop more.
Slides 2 and 3 both argue 'the tool saved time', so the headline arc repeats instead of advancing. How do I split them?
problems.explanation: The note names a concrete structural fault (a repeated headline claim) so feedback can target the arc.

problems.stem: How can you use AI on slide structure without handing over your judgment?
options: Ask AI to apply a flashy template and call the deck finished.
Paste your six slide headlines and ask AI whether the arc has gaps or repeats, then you decide what to reorder.
Ask AI to write all the body text so you do not have to think about the message.
Use AI only to add transitions between slides.
problems.explanation: AI critiques the headline arc as a proposal; you keep the decision about ordering and message.

problems.stem: A peer says your slide 'has no point.' Which revision fixes the structure first?
options: Add an animated chart and a brighter color.
Rewrite the title from 'Results' to the assertion 'Response time dropped from 4.2s to 1.1s after caching.'
Add more bullet points to fill the slide.
problems.explanation: An assertion headline gives the slide a single inspectable point before any decoration is considered.
